page: Microsoft Azure D32_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture and powered by an Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C processor clocked at 2.8 GHz. The instance delivers 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores using multithreading, backed by 48 MB of L3 cache. It incorporates 128 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware instruction support includes AVX-512 with VNNI extensions, AES, and VAES cryptographic acceleration, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The virtual machine does not include bundled local disk storage or dedicated GPUs.

Benchmark testing situates the instance largely within middle-tier performance parameters across general compute metrics. PassMark CPU scored 36,815.64 and Geekbench multi-core achieved 13,894.0, demonstrating balanced multi-threaded execution for compilation and standard compute tasks. PassMark memory testing exhibited strong results at 2,794.18, aligning with uncached read memory bandwidth of 134.75 GB/sec and small-block cached throughput exceeding 1,600 GB/sec. Static web serving throughput reached 32.99 GB/sec alongside 31.41 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations. For machine learning, small model inference (135M) showed solid throughput, whereas large 70B parameter prompt processing dropped into the bottom quartile at 6.57 tokens per second due to the absence of hardware accelerators.

The D32_v5 provides a consistent compute profile for mainstream enterprise workloads that do not demand dedicated GPUs or ephemeral scratch disks. Because instance storage relies entirely on attached remote network volumes, I/O design must account for remote disk latencies. This hardware allocation fits mid-sized relational databases, distributed caching nodes, CI/CD build environments, and containerized enterprise applications requiring reliable memory density and balanced multi-core performance.
description: Microsoft Azure D32_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine equipped with 32 vCPUs and 128 GB of RAM running on a 2.8 GHz Intel Xeon 8370C processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture with Hyper-V virtualization, it offers 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading and 48 MB of L3 cache. The instance features a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory configuration and supports AVX-512 VNNI instructions. There is no integrated local storage or discrete GPU hardware, necessitating external block storage for persistent data. Benchmark metrics reflect solid middle-tier CPU and multi-threading capabilities, complemented by strong memory subsystem scores and high-throughput Redis caching performance. Due to its balanced memory and compute density, the D32_v5 is well suited for enterprise application servers, memory-intensive caching tiers, CI/CD compilation pipelines, and container orchestration nodes.
